subject: Re: SIG evidence request — SDLC artifacts for code review, CI/CD and secrets
messages:
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme-corp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG: request for SDLC artifacts - code review, CI/CD, secrets handling

Hi Tessa,

Acme's assessment team is running a SIG review and we need to collect evidence for a few Secure SDLC controls related to your service. Specifically we're after:

- Traceability from commits -> PR -> CI run -> release (artifact IDs or run IDs),
- Code review enforcement: branch protections, PR reviewer counts, required approvals, and a sample of PR reviews for a recent release,
- CI/CD controls: runner identities, ephemeral vs persistent runners, artifacts retention and provenance, and a list of job IDs for the release window,
- Secrets management: KMS/HSM usage, rotation cadence for service keys, and any ephemeral secret practices in the pipeline,
- Change management: approval evidence for the last three production deploys (ticket IDs, approval logs, and rollback runbooks).

Can you produce a single package with the items above and a short mapping doc that points an assessor to each artifact (where to find it and how to validate)? Our deadline for the SIG submission is 2028-10-13, so if we could have an initial bundle by 2028-10-09 that would be great.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Johnson
Senior Security Assessor, Acme Financial
security@acme-corp.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-01T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: request for SDLC artifacts - code review, CI/CD, secrets handling

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We're happy to assemble this. High-level comment on what we'll provide in the package and where it's coming from:

- Commits -> release mapping: signed commit manifest (repo-commit-manifest.csv) listing commit SHAs, PR numbers, CI run IDs, and generated release artifact IDs. We will include signed checksum for the manifest.
- PR/Code review evidence: pr-review-matrix.xlsx with per-PR reviewers, timestamps, and the branch-protection policy snapshot we enforce.
- CI provenance: ci-run-ids.jsonl with referenced CI job IDs for the release window, runner labels (ephemeral vs dedicated), and links to raw CI job output stored in our secure audit bucket.
- Secrets/KMS: kms-rotation-statement.txt with last rotation timestamps, KMS key IDs, and the KMS audit query we ran (export attached).
- Change approvals: deployment-approval-logs.pdf with the approval audit trail (who approved, ticket ids), plus the change advisory minutes from ENGOPS-1423.

One clarification: for some CI logs we can provide an export of job metadata (IDs, runner identity, exit code) but not full redacted logs in-line. If the assessor needs a live walkthrough to validate log provenance, we can schedule a 45-minute session.

We'll aim to deliver the initial bundle by 2028-10-09 EOD Pacific and can follow up with the walkthrough the week of 2028-10-10. Monica will coordinate artifact collection; Ben will provide the KMS statements.

Action items: Monica, Ben — please collect the artifacts and drop in the Drive folder and ping Alice for access.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: request for SDLC artifacts - code review, CI/CD, secrets handling

Forwarding internal collection notes:

--- internal note ---
Planned artifacts and source locations: 
1) repo-commit-manifest.csv — generated via our release automation (script: tools/release/manifest-gen.py). Manifest includes signed SHA256 per-commit and the GPG signature of the manifest. Stored in GCS bucket: gs://redwood-evidence/acme/2028-10-09/.

2) pr-review-matrix.xlsx — produced by a query against GitHub API + review webhook logs (we require 1+ code owner approval and block on failed checks). Snapshot of branch protection rules exported via GH API and included.

3) ci-run-ids.jsonl — exported from our CI system (BuildGrid) listing job_id, run_id, timestamp, runner_label, commit_sha, and artifact_id. Runners are mixed: ephemeral (k8s) vs dedicated (self-hosted). We will mark which are ephemeral.

4) kms-rotation-statement.txt — KMS key metadata exported from our cloud KMS (key IDs, last rotation, and the rotation schedule). Ben will also export the KMS audit query we used for the period.

5) deployment-approval-logs.pdf & change-advisory-minutes-ENGOPS-1423.pdf — approval logs are produced by our change request tool (ticket ENGOPS-1423). We will include the approval e-mails, who approved, and time stamps. Rollback playbook is cross-referenced in the minutes.

Notes: commits are signed by developer keys; we enforce branch protections (required status checks, signed commits optional but recommended). For the assessment we can provide a sample of three PR threads that cover the last three production deploys.

I'll place everything in the Drive folder and post the links. Also created a Jira ticket for traceability: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/ENGOPS-1423.

-Monica
Engineering Manager, Release Reliability

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme-corp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2028-10-05T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: request for SDLC artifacts - code review, CI/CD, secrets handling

Thanks, Tessa and Monica — that plan sounds good. Two quick asks before you send the bundle:

1) Can we have a short (30–45 min) walkthrough of the manifest and CI provenance on 2028-10-10 or 2028-10-11? We want to verify the signing keys and the linkage from PR -> CI -> artifact.
2) Please redline any artifacts that contain sensitive data; where full logs are not provided, a small excerpt plus the job metadata is sufficient.

If you can confirm a walkthrough time and that the Drive folder will be accessible by our assessor (alice.johnson@acme-corp.com), we'll plan to review.

Regards,
Alice

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-09T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: request for SDLC artifacts - code review, CI/CD, secrets handling

Alice — bundle uploaded and access granted to your address (Drive link below). Summary of what we included and quick guidance for the assessor:

Attachments included in this e-mail and the Drive folder:
- repo-commit-manifest.csv (signed manifest; columns: commit_sha, pr_number, ci_run_id, artifact_id, manifest_signature)
- ci-run-ids.jsonl (metadata-only export; no raw logs)
- pr-review-matrix.xlsx (three PR samples tied to the release)
- kms-rotation-statement.txt (rotation dates and KMS key IDs)
- deployment-approval-logs.pdf (approval audit trail)
- change-advisory-minutes-ENGOPS-1423.pdf (CAB minutes, approvals and rollback decision points)

Quick notes:
- The manifest is GPG signed by our release user (release-bot@redwood.com). To validate, verify the manifest_signature and the public key fingerprint: 3F2B 7A9C 11D4 8A2E 45B1  C2F9 9A8E 21B3.
- CI exports include run IDs that map to the manifest; run metadata shows runner_label: "ephemeral-k8s" for ephemeral CI and "self-hosted-gpu" for dedicated.
- KMS statement includes last rotation dates for keys used by CI to unwrap secrets during runs. No secret material is included in the export.

Walkthrough availability: Tessa & Monica are available 2028-10-10 10:00–11:00 PT or 2028-10-11 14:00–15:00 PT. Please confirm which slot works for you.

Drive link (internal access): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cSDLCEvidence
Jira ticket for traceability: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/ENGOPS-1423

If you need additional artifacts (e.g., raw CI logs for a specific run) we can provide a redacted extract under a separate NDA exchange.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
